topic: The 50/30/20 budget: about 50% of take-home pay for needs, 30% for wants and 20% for savings, as a simple starting point.

episode.title: The 50/30/20 Budget: Three Simple Buckets

shots.narration: Payday already feels confusing? Coin has a simple starting point.
shots.scene: Bright modern flat, vertical 9:16 3D animation, scattered plain gold tokens beside groceries and a takeaway cup on a table; no text or lettering.
shots.action: Kash scratches her head over the scattered tokens.
shots.mood: Sunny yellow lighting, puzzled expression, friendly rounded shapes.

shots.narration: Try 50/30/20: needs, wants, and savings from take-home pay.
shots.scene: Same table with three empty transparent jars bearing only pictograms: a grocery basket, a café cup, and a piggy bank; no text.
shots.action: Coin sweeps one tiny arm across the three jars.
shots.mood: Bright teal and mustard palette, welcoming smiles, clear uncluttered layout.

shots.narration: [excited] For example, imagine taking home 100 coins.
shots.scene: Vertical 3D view of the flat's table, ten neat stacks of ten plain gold tokens beside the empty pictogram jars; no text.
shots.action: Kash places a tray holding the ten stacks onto the table.
shots.mood: Warm daylight, delighted expressions, orderly shiny tokens.

shots.narration: About 50 coins go toward needs, like groceries.
shots.scene: Close view of the grocery-basket jar and the tray of gold tokens in the bright flat; no text or numerals.
shots.action: Coin slides five ten-token stacks into the wide grocery-basket jar.
shots.mood: Fresh green accents, reassuring smile, crisp readable shapes.

shots.narration: Then 30 coins cover wants, like café treats.
shots.scene: Close view of the café-cup jar beside a small pastry, with five token stacks remaining on the tray; no text.
shots.action: Coin slides three ten-token stacks into the wide café-cup jar.
shots.mood: Soft coral accents, cheerful expression, cozy café-inspired details.

shots.scene: Close view of the piggy-bank jar and the final two token stacks on the tray; bright modern flat, no text.
shots.action: Coin slides the final two ten-token stacks into the wide piggy-bank jar.
shots.mood: Sky-blue accents, sparkling gold highlights, pleased smile.

shots.narration: It's a simple starting point, not a strict rule.
shots.scene: All three jars on the table, holding five, three, and two equal token stacks respectively; pictograms only, no lettering.
shots.action: Coin presents the three-jar arrangement with open arms.
shots.mood: Relaxed posture, gentle smiles, balanced pastel composition.

shots.narration: Now Kash can see needs, wants, and savings separately.
shots.scene: Tidy flat table with the three filled pictogram jars aligned beside Kash's small blank notebook; no text.
shots.action: Kash nods toward the neatly separated jars.
shots.mood: Bright afternoon light, relieved smile, calm uncluttered surroundings.

shots.narration: [excited] Sketch three buckets today; next, we'll sort needs from wants.
shots.scene: Close view of Kash's notebook beside the grocery-basket and café-cup jars, vertical 3D frame; no text, letters, or numerals.
shots.action: Kash draws three simple bucket outlines in her notebook.
shots.mood: Warm inviting light, curious smiles, playful anticipation.

episode.endHook: Next episode: how do you tell needs from wants?
episode.description: Coin helps Kash explore the 50/30/20 budget: about 50% of take-home pay for needs, 30% for wants, and 20% for savings. Follow a simple 100-coin example, then sketch your own three buckets today. General money education, not personal financial advice.
